description: The agent must: (1) Read all three input files to understand the arguments, dates, and team. (2) Apply SKILL.md's ~21 min total / ~10 min per claim time allocation rule. (3) Order Claim 1 sub-arguments with ARBITRARY DETENTION (C1-B, strongest/substantive) first, then FAIR TRIAL elements (C1-D, broader doctrinal bridge) before REASONS FOR ARREST (C1-C), and procedural LAWFULNESS (C1-A) last — matching the Kafker-style ordering principle in SKILL.md. (4) Order Claim 2 with RISK OF TORTURE (C2-B) first, BURDEN OF PROOF (C2-D) immediately after as a doctrinal bridge, EFFECTIVE REMEDY (C2-C) next, and DIPLOMATIC ASSURANCES (C2-A, weakest) either omitted or placed last. (5) Note that weaknesses should only be addressed if asked by judges — not proactively. (6) Correctly compute that the gap from 2025-03-10 to 2025-04-05 is 26 days (< 30 days threshold), so the 30-day exception does NOT apply and high-frequency mocking must start immediately: every 2 days in the early phase (Mar 10–21), then every 1 day in the late phase (Mar 22–Apr 4), plus one session immediately before each major round. (7) Configure each mock session with exactly 1 oralist, 1–3 judges (who must record improvable points), 1 timekeeper, and 1 separate question recorder — all drawn from the team roster.
